newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African budget: probe seeks tax on trust capital.
newsitem.headline: S.African budget: probe seeks tax on trust capital.

text.p: The South African government is studying a report recommending a transfer tax on the distribution of capital from trusts as part of its overhaul of tax legislation.

According to the budget review released with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget speech on Wednesday, some of the issues now under review by the Katz commission included capital transfer tax and taxes on land, benefit funds, mining and non-governmental organisations.
A draft report on capital transfers had recommended that donations tax and estate duty should be retained separately.
"The distribution of capital from trusts should generally be subject to the impostion of capital transfer tax and sensible provision should be made for transition," the commission has proposed.
No specific legislation was needed to remedy problems associated with interest-free loans and preference shares and no general anti-avoidance legislation was favoured.
The commission recommended special provisions to deal with "generation-skipping trusts" and the present exemption from estate duty for bequests in favour of surviving spouses should remain.
The Katz report should be released to the public soon, the review said.
A report on the imposition of a land tax at local (municipal) government level was expected to be ready in late 1997.
A report on all aspects of mining taxation, including the taxation of mineral rights, should be ready in the first half this year.
The commission had submitted a provisional report on whether tax should be imposed on income regardless of its source, or on income at source regardless of the residence of the recipient.

The review said the tax advisory committee had consulted a wide range of organisations on issues such as the abuse of fringe benefits tax, the implicit tax benefits of the so-called "Voyager card" system of credit rewards for spending and the status of joint venture companies under a tax holiday scheme announced last year.
It was also planned to simplify the Income Tax Act to ensure that it was clearer on certain issues and easier to understand.
Progress had also been made in concluding double taxation agreements, which were now in place with 28 countries with others being negotiated.
The review said that it had also been proposed that greater use should be made of tax reference numbers to help the South African Revenue Services fight tax evasion.
